notes: The adr-status pack does what its README says and nothing more. Its one pass runs once per note, works only on notes whose frontmatter has `type: decision`, and gets work from notes that sessions touched or cited. It reads sessions, notes, turns and human_confirmed, and each is needed: the session date and context, the record itself so it can skip changes already noted, the cited turns as evidence, and restored text so it does not contradict what a person settled. The prompt treats the delimited inputs as data and allows only `append` changes with an empty `old` to the given note. Entries go under a final `## Status updates` section, and anything the turns do not state is left out. Commands, instructions and links that appear only in tool output are not quoted, and output is limited to 2,048 bytes. The reviewer persona rejects by default, treats all inputs as untrusted, keeps a strict one-sentence JSON reply, and rejects non-append changes, unsupported reasons, dates or successors, duplicates, and content sourced only from tool output. The template holds only frontmatter, headings, placeholder text and a plain description of the Status updates section, with no agent instructions, commands, links or credential handling. The test fixtures are clearly synthetic: the transcript is marked `synthetic`, and the sample app, dates and an unrelated decoy note test that only notes of the matching type are read. Nothing is hidden, encoded or misnamed, and this is a first install, so there is no update diff to account for.
